 MOF Studying Potential Refund Of RM377m Nicotine Vape Tax After Court Ruling
 By CodeBlue | 
 18 November 2026 
 MOF is studying a potential need to refund vape businesses RM377 million in excise duties collected on nicotine vapes after a High Court ruling six months ago. Finance Minister Anwar says MOF is seeking MOH’s response on the direction of vape products. 
 The Finance Ministry’s headquarters in Putrajaya. Photo by Shutterstock. 
 KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is still looking at whether the government needs to refund excise duties collected on nicotine-containing vape liquids after a High Court ruling six months ago.
 According to MOF, the government has collected RM377.08 million in excise duties on nicotine vape products and liquid and gel nicotine to date, since tax enforcement began on May 1, 2023, and that the money has already been transferred to the federal consolidated fund.
 “In relation to your question on whether the collection will be returned to vape industry players following the Kuala Lumpur High Court ruling, the government’s priority now is on a comprehensive of the legal implications of that judgment and follow-up measures that need to be taken by the government,” said Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim in a written Dewan Rakyat reply to Kuala Langat MP Dr Ahmad Yunus Hairi yesterday.
 “At the same time, the Finance Ministry is also seeking a response from the Ministry of Health (MOH) on the direction of vape products to enable further perusal by MOF of tax-related issues.”
 In a landmark ruling on May 15 , the High Court nullified a 2023 exemption order by then-Health Minister Dr Zaliha Mustafa to remove liquid and gel nicotine used in e-cigarettes and vapes from the Poisons List. The exemption was made to enable taxation. 
 The government later withdrew its appeal against the High Court ruling in August.
 MOF secretary-general Johan Mahmood Merican previously said in a 2023 affidavit in the case that cancelling the 2023 nicotine exemption would invalidate the government’s collection of excise duties on nicotine-containing vape liquids.
 Health Minister Dzulkefly Ahmad told Parliament recently that nicotine e-liquids are once again a scheduled poison subject to the Poisons Act 1952 (Act 366), as a result of the High Court verdict.
 He has yet to gazette a new nicotine exemption order after the Poisons Board endorsed his proposal for the exemption.
 The health minister also has yet to explain whether the Madani administration intends to ban vape, as per his declaration last year, or if Putrajaya is seeking to regularise nicotine vape products once more to continue obtaining tax revenue.
